concerns.text: Success Criterion SC-008 (Baseline model training success) does not reference any User Story. It only cites FR-007, which itself is anchored to US-03, but SC-008 lacks a direct story anchor, making it an orphaned success criterion.

"System MUST generate a sufficiently large set of synthetic video sequences..." lacks a quantitative definition of "sufficiently large" (e.g., exact number of sequences or total duration), making the requirement untestable.
Success Criteria SC-003 specifies thresholds for SSIM and LPIPS but omits any measurable threshold for PSNR, even though PSNR is listed as a required evaluation metric in FR-004 and US‑03.

The deterministic reproducibility claim (identical results on repeated runs with the same seed) does not describe a concrete verification procedure (e.g., compare file hashes or checksum of rendered frames), leaving the test ambiguous.

The validation metric (SSIM/LPIPS) compares the student model’s output to the ground‑truth physics frames that are themselves generated by the deterministic physics engine used as the teacher signal (FR‑001). Because the predictor (physics trajectory) and the validation target (physics frames) are derived from the same deterministic process, the evaluation is not independent and constitutes a circular validation of the core hypothesis.

The paired t‑test on SSIM and LPIPS scores (SC‑004) assumes independent, normally‑distributed paired observations, yet both models are trained and evaluated on the same synthetic dataset. This makes the observations non‑independent and violates the assumptions of the t‑test, rendering the claimed statistical significance potentially invalid.

The assumption of ≥ 0.8 statistical power for the paired t‑test is stated without a concrete sample‑size or effect‑size calculation. A proper power analysis (e.g., specifying number of test sequences, expected effect size, and variance) is required to justify the claim.
